text:
incident-bot: 🚨 [INCIDENT] probe-swing routing misdirect detected across regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Ongoing since 2026-02-15T14:20:34Z. High error-rate on short-lived requests, elevated latency, some 5xxs. Auto-escalating to on-call.

pagerduty: Paging ryan_oncall and maya_oncall for high-severity routing loop. @ryan_oncall / @maya_oncall pls ack.

ryan_oncall: ack. I'm on it. Looking at routing logs now.

alex_runtime: I see KL divergence in health probes: node-level probe in eu flips pass/fail every 8-12s, triggers regional failover, then us-west experiences similar probe oscillation. Looks like a short TTL on probe cooldown + route fallback cascade.

tess_sre: can you paste the probe logs? want the exact pattern.

alex_runtime: paste logs:
```
2026-02-15T14:19:58Z eu/probe check=PASS latency=12ms
2026-02-15T14:20:06Z eu/probe check=FAIL latency=300ms err=timeout
2026-02-15T14:20:14Z eu/probe check=PASS latency=14ms
2026-02-15T14:20:22Z eu/probe check=FAIL latency=400ms err=connection-reset
```
Also saw similar timestamps on us-west after routing change.

maya_oncall: That 8s cadence matches our cheap healthcheck debounce (10s sample window, immediate failover). If probes are flaky under transient network jitter, the routing engine flip-flops.

priya_prod_support: Customer impact: a handful of PLG customers in EU saw spikes in error rates and partial request timeouts for ~6 minutes. One enterprise customer (acct_id: acct-412) reported degraded UX for internal search. No data loss.

jordan_cs: notified customer success; they escalated to account team. Keeping them updated.

ryan_oncall: Immediate mitigation: I'm going to temporarily increase healthprobe "failure_threshold" and add a 30s cooldown on regional failover for the affected routing policy. Also will disable automatic model-variant crossover for the route until stable.

deploy-bot: Received config change request from ryan_oncall. Applying to routing-config/prod/policies/service-llm: set failure_threshold=3 -> 6, failover_cooldown=30s.

deploy-bot: Change applied (config-rollback available). Rolling config across controllers in us-east/us-west/eu.

tess_sre: Good. Also suggest pausing cross-region quick-failover and mark eu as "deprioritized" for non-SLA customers until probes stabilize.

maya_oncall: I'm going to run the hotfix: route-policy set "sticky_preference": true for the default service so we avoid bounce. Command:
```
redwoodctl routing update --policy service-llm --set sticky_preference=true --set failover_cooldown=30s
```

alex_runtime: After hotfix, I'm seeing probe noise still in eu but the routing thrash stops. Latency for in-flight requests drops back to baseline. Adding a temporary higher weight to us-east to absorb traffic.

priya_prod_support: Monitoring: error-rate for affected customers decreased from 8.2% -> 0.6% in 45s. Still watching.

jordan_cs: Customers on the thread acknowledged reduced errors. Account team will wait for stability before lifting mitigations.

tess_sre: Root cause hypothesis: an upgrade last night to the eu probe agent bumped its connection pool and introduced short-lived TCP resets under load. The short probe debounce + immediate failover triggered a three-way swing. Need postmortem with the agent diff.

ryan_oncall: Agreed. Next steps: 1) keep cooldown in place for 2 hours, 2) revert probe-agent change in eu to previous build (canary) and monitor, 3) open postmortem ticket and assign owner, 4) notify infra/network about possible packet drops.

priya_prod_support: I'll prepare the customer update template. ETA 20m.

alex_runtime: Rolling back probe agent on eu canary now. Command:
```
depoyctl rollback --cluster=eu --service=probe-agent --to=release-2026-02-10
```

deploy-bot: Rollback queued; will notify on completion.

deploy-bot: Rollback completed on eu canary (instance group a). Monitoring for probe stability.

maya_oncall: eu probe logs after rollback:
```
2026-02-15T14:25:12Z eu/probe check=PASS latency=13ms
2026-02-15T14:25:40Z eu/probe check=PASS latency=15ms
2026-02-15T14:26:08Z eu/probe check=PASS latency=12ms
```
Looks stable so far.

tess_sre: Good. Assigning PM for postmortem: @alex_runtime will own. Postmortem ticket created: INC-2026-5123. Include timeline, config diffs, and customer impact.

ryan_oncall: I'll keep the failover_cooldown and sticky_preference for 2 hours, then we'll revert to normal once we've had 30m of stable metrics.

priya_prod_support: Customer update draft ready, sending to legal/ops for signoff, then will publish.

jordan_cs: Notified account team. They will send a short note to the affected customer within 30m.

incident-bot: Severity downgraded to medium at 2026-02-15T14:33:00Z after routing stabilization. Continue monitoring.

ryan_oncall: Closing the active page at my end, leaving follow-ups: INC-2026-5123 (postmortem), TASK-7891 (probe-agent root cause), CONFIG-4321 (routing policy cooldown default change). If oscillation returns, page SRE immediately.

maya_oncall: ack. Great work team. :thumbsup:

priya_prod_support: Logging customer-impact summary to the incident ticket: ~6 minutes of elevated errors for subset of EU customers, mitigated by routing cooldown and probe rollback. No data loss, no SLA breach reported yet.

alex_runtime: I'll author the postmortem and include the suggested long-term changes: add exponential backoff for probe flapping, increase default cooldown, and more robust probe telemetry.

tess_sre: Thanks everyone. Closing live thread; we'll reconvene in the postmortem channel tomorrow.
